title: U.S. House · Texas's 19th District
area: West Texas, including Lubbock and Abilene.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Jodey Arrington did not appear on the ballot in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the redrawn 19th District. Tom Sell won the Republican nomination in a May 26, 2026 primary runoff over Abraham Enriquez after leading a seven-candidate March primary field. Kyle Rable ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination.

candidates.name: Tom Sell
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 26, 2026 Republican primary runoff over Abraham Enriquez, 64.3% to 35.7%.

summary.text: Tom Sell is the Republican nominee for this open West Texas seat. A Lubbock resident who describes himself as a fifth-generation West Texan, he worked for former U.S. Rep. Larry Combest, served as deputy staff director of the House Agriculture Committee, and has run the Lubbock firm Combest, Sell & Associates for about 21 years. He won the Republican primary runoff on May 26, 2026, with 64.3% of the vote.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a fifth-generation West Texan; his family moved to Lubbock as sharecroppers in 1906, according to The Texas Tribune. USA Rice Daily reports he was born and raised in the 19th District, where he met his wife, Kyla.
Earned a bachelor's degree and a J.D. from Texas Tech University; his campaign website says the bachelor's was in agribusiness.

Worked in the office of former U.S. Rep. Larry Combest (R-Texas) and served as deputy staff director for the House Committee on Agriculture, which Combest chaired, from 1999 to early 2003, according to The Texas Tribune.
According to his campaign website, he helped advance the Crop Insurance Reform Act of 2000 and the 2002 Farm Bill while working for Combest.

After leaving Capitol Hill, returned to Lubbock and founded the firm now called Combest, Sell & Associates with Combest; he has run it for about 21 years, according to USA Rice Daily. Opponent Jason Corley, in the Republican primary, called him a "career lobbyist."
Ran in the 2026 Republican primary for the open 19th District seat; he led the seven-candidate March 3 field with 40.4% and defeated Abraham Enriquez in the May 26 runoff, 64.3% to 35.7%.

Lives in Lubbock with his wife, Kyla; the couple raised four children, and their campaign site says they are active in their church and community and mentor students at Texas Tech's Davis College of Agriculture. The Tribune reports he has coached Little League.

candidates.researchNotes: A campaign website (selltexastrue.com) was found; no Candidate Connection survey was located.

candidates.name: Kyle Rable
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed for the Democratic nomination, winning the March 3, 2026 primary with 100% of the vote.

summary.text: Kyle Rable is the Democratic nominee for this open West Texas seat. A captain in the U.S. Army Reserve and a Texas Tech Ph.D. candidate who lives in Lubbock, he has served as secretary of the Lubbock County Democratic Party. Local news reports his website's priorities as West Texas farms and rural communities, Medicare and Medicaid, and monopolies.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he comes from a family of working-class people and immigrants with a military background, and worked in restaurants and kitchens to support himself through school.
Attended the University of Toledo on an Army ROTC scholarship, per his campaign website, and later earned a graduate degree from Bowling Green State University.
Received a commission in the U.S. Army Reserve and continued serving as an Army officer while earning his master's degree; he is a captain in the Reserve.
Entered the Ph.D. program at Texas Tech University, where he is described as a Ph.D. candidate.
According to his campaign website, he is a member of CWA Local 6186 and advocated with the union in Austin against SB17 and SB18 during the 2023 legislative session.
Served as secretary of the Lubbock County Democratic Party, according to KCBD in 2025.
Announced his candidacy for Texas's 19th District in May 2025; as of November 2025 he was the only person to have filed in the Democratic primary.
Lives in Lubbock with his wife, Kristen, their son and two rescue dogs, according to his campaign website.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website rableforwesttexas.com has a short biography; no Candidate Connection survey was located.

researchNotes: This is an open seat after Texas redrew its congressional map for 2026; incumbent Jodey Arrington did not run in the redrawn 19th District's primary. Neither general-election nominee has completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or published detailed policy positions online. Biographies draw on candidate websites and local news; neither nominee's birth year is published in the sources reviewed.
